questions.stem: Which of the following is a basic characteristic of West African Traditional Religion?
options: It is spread mainly by missionaries
It is based on one written holy book
It teaches that God does not exist
It has no single human founder
questions.explanation: W.A.T.R. grew out of the life and experience of the people over generations, so it has no known founder, missionaries or written scripture.

questions.topic: Purpose of the study of W.A.T.R.
questions.stem: One important reason for studying West African Traditional Religion in schools is to
options: prepare learners to become priests of a shrine
help learners understand and appreciate their cultural heritage
replace Christianity and Islam in the society
prove that the religion is superior to others
questions.explanation: The study aims at understanding and appreciation of the culture and values that shape West African life, not at conversion or ranking religions.

questions.topic: Terms Used to Describe West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: Early foreign writers described W.A.T.R. as 'fetishism'. This term is considered wrong mainly because the worshippers
options: do not worship the objects themselves but the spiritual beings they represent
have no objects at all in their worship
worship only the Supreme Being directly
do not believe in spiritual beings
questions.explanation: Objects such as carved figures are symbols; worship is directed to the spiritual beings behind them, so 'fetishism' misrepresents the religion.

questions.topic: Terms Used to Describe West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: A scholar argues that W.A.T.R. is best described as 'diffused monotheism'. He means that
options: there is one Supreme God whose authority is shared out among divinities who act as his ministers
there are many equal gods with no supreme head
God has handed over the world entirely and no longer acts
every person is regarded as a god
questions.explanation: Diffused monotheism (associated with Bolaji Idowu) holds that God is one and supreme, while divinities derive their power from him.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-oral source of W.A.T.R.?
options: Carved wooden masks used at festivals
questions.explanation: Arts and crafts such as carvings, masks, paintings and shrines are non-oral; proverbs, myths and names are oral sources.

questions.stem: Names such as Oluwaseun, Chukwuemeka and Nyamekye, which contain a reference to God, are called
questions.explanation: Theophorous names carry the name of God or a divinity and show people's belief about God.

questions.stem: A proverb says, 'It is God who drives away flies for the tailless animal.' The belief expressed here is that God is
questions.explanation: The proverb teaches that God provides for the helpless, an attribute of providence and care.

questions.topic: Approaches to the Study of West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: A student studies how three different West African peoples conduct burial rites in order to note their similarities and differences. This is the
questions.explanation: Comparing practices across peoples is the comparative approach.

questions.topic: Approaches to the Study of West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: The main weakness of the enumerative approach to the study of W.A.T.R. is that it
options: is too short to be useful
merely lists the beliefs and practices of many peoples without showing how they fit together
questions.explanation: Enumeration catalogues many beliefs one after another, often superficially, without integrating or analysing them.

questions.stem: In many West African societies there are few or no shrines or priests dedicated directly to the Supreme Being. This is mainly because
options: the people do not believe in God
God is thought to be too great to be confined to a shrine and is approached through intermediaries
God is worshipped only by chiefs
questions.explanation: God is seen as transcendent and great; divinities and ancestors serve as intermediaries, though people may pray to God directly at any time.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions must a dead person usually satisfy to become an ancestor?
options: He must have died young in a war
He must have been very wealthy
He must have lived a morally good life and died a good death at old age
He must have been buried outside his community
questions.explanation: Ancestorhood requires a good life, old age, children and a proper burial; a bad death disqualifies.

questions.stem: Sango among the Yoruba is associated with
options: farming and fertility of the soil
questions.explanation: Sango is the Yoruba divinity of thunder and lightning.

questions.stem: An object worn on the body or hung at the entrance of a house to protect the owner from evil is
questions.explanation: Amulets and talismans are protective objects; a libation is an offering poured out.

questions.stem: Pouring drink or water on the ground while calling on the ancestors is known as
questions.explanation: Libation is prayer accompanied by pouring a liquid offering.

questions.stem: A sacrifice offered to restore a broken relationship with a divinity after a taboo has been violated is
questions.explanation: Propitiation appeases an offended spiritual being; votive fulfils a vow; thanksgiving expresses gratitude.

questions.stem: During a festival a priestess falls into a trance and begins to speak in a different voice, giving messages to the worshippers. This is
questions.explanation: Spirit possession is when a divinity is believed to take over a medium to communicate with people.

questions.topic: Religious Personalities in West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: A person who discovers hidden knowledge and the will of the spirits through means such as Ifa or kola nuts is
questions.explanation: Diviners interpret the will of the spiritual world through divination systems.

questions.topic: Festivals in West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: The New Yam festival common among the Igbo is mainly
options: a mourning ceremony for a dead king
a thanksgiving for a good harvest
questions.explanation: The New Yam festival thanks the divinities and ancestors for the harvest before the new yams are eaten.

questions.stem: The traditional medical practitioner who uses mainly leaves, roots and barks of plants to treat illness is
questions.explanation: Herbalists use plant materials for healing.

questions.stem: One major weakness of traditional healing compared with orthodox (hospital) medicine is that
options: it is not available in rural areas
the dosage of many herbal preparations is not measured accurately
questions.explanation: Lack of standard dosage and hygiene control is a common criticism; traditional medicine is usually cheaper and more accessible.

questions.stem: In traditional West African thought, time is mainly understood as
options: a mathematical figure on a clock
a thing that has no relation to events
a commodity that is bought and sold
a series of events that have occurred or are about to occur
questions.explanation: Time is reckoned by events (seasons, market days, festivals) rather than by abstract numbers.

questions.stem: According to W.A.T.R., wealth acquired through dishonest means is
options: a sign of the blessing of God
acceptable if shared with the chief
likely to bring punishment from the ancestors and divinities
questions.explanation: Wealth is good when honestly acquired; ill-gotten wealth attracts spiritual sanction.

questions.stem: Many West African peoples believe that a human being is made up of
options: a physical body and a spiritual element given by God
only a spirit with no body
the body of an animal and a tree
questions.explanation: Man is seen as body plus soul/breath (e.g. okan, emi, ori among the Yoruba) given by God.

questions.stem: Among the Yoruba the concept of destiny is closely linked with
questions.explanation: Ori (the inner head) is associated with personal destiny chosen before birth.

questions.stem: The difference between magic and witchcraft in West African belief is that magic
options: is always inherited from the mother
uses words and objects and can be used for good or for harm
is practised only at night by spirits
questions.explanation: Magic is a technique using materials and incantations, positive or negative; witchcraft is an inner, usually evil power.

questions.stem: Spirits believed to cause misfortune such as accidents and madness are called
questions.explanation: Malevolent spirits are evil spirits that bring harm.

questions.topic: Religion and Ethics in West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: Two families resolve a long-standing quarrel by sharing kola nut and taking an oath before the ancestors never to harm each other again. This is an example of
questions.explanation: A covenant is a solemn agreement sealed with ritual and witnessed by spiritual beings.

questions.topic: Stages of the rites of passage
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a rite of passage?
questions.explanation: Rites of passage mark the stages of an individual's life; planting season is an agricultural period.

questions.stem: An important function of puberty rites is that they
options: give a person the title of chief
mark the passage from childhood to adulthood and teach adult responsibilities
questions.explanation: Puberty/initiation rites transfer the young into adulthood with education on roles and morals.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a religious function of a traditional chief in West Africa?
options: Collecting income tax for the federal government
Performing or overseeing rituals on behalf of the community
Appointing judges of the supreme court
questions.explanation: Traditional rulers are sacred figures who lead or sponsor community rituals and festivals.

questions.stem: Asafo companies are traditional institutions associated mainly with
questions.explanation: Asafo companies are warrior groups of the Fante (and other Akan) peoples of Ghana.

questions.stem: How can traditional religious festivals contribute to tourism?
options: They prevent foreigners from entering the community
They discourage the building of hotels
They attract visitors who spend money in the local economy
questions.explanation: Festivals such as Osun-Osogbo draw visitors and boost local income.

questions.stem: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in
questions.explanation: The Osun-Osogbo grove, inscribed by UNESCO in 2005, is in Osogbo, Osun State.

questions.topic: Religion and Stress Management in West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: Which of the following is a traditional way of managing stress caused by the death of a loved one?
options: Communal mourning rites in which relatives and neighbours support the bereaved
Leaving the bereaved alone in the house
Sending the bereaved away from the community
questions.explanation: Communal support and rituals help the bereaved cope with grief.

questions.topic: The Role of W.A.T.R. in Conflict Resolution and Management
questions.stem: In traditional West African society, a common method of settling a land dispute between two families is
options: arbitration by elders and the chief, sometimes with an oath before a divinity
questions.explanation: Elders and chiefs mediate disputes; oaths before divinities ensure truth-telling.

questions.stem: A health concern often raised about traditional circumcision rites in West Africa is
options: that the rites are performed in hospitals
that they are too expensive for families
infection resulting from the use of unsterilised instruments
that they are performed only on adults
questions.explanation: Non-sterile instruments can spread infections such as tetanus and HIV; female genital cutting is also widely condemned as harmful.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of Christianity and Islam on W.A.T.R.?
options: Traditional festivals ceased to exist everywhere
W.A.T.R. began to use written scriptures
Many converts abandoned shrines and traditional festivals
questions.explanation: Conversion reduced participation in traditional worship, though many festivals survive.

questions.stem: The traditional practice of protecting certain forests as sacred groves helps
options: the conservation of plants and animals
questions.explanation: Restrictions on entering or cutting sacred groves preserve biodiversity.

questions.stem: Godianism, a religious movement in Nigeria, was founded by
questions.explanation: Chief K. O. K. Onyioha founded Godianism in 1948 to promote belief in the God of Africa.

questions.topic: The future of West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to help W.A.T.R. survive in the future?
options: The study of the religion in schools and the preservation of festivals and sacred sites
questions.explanation: Education, documentation and preservation of festivals and sites help the religion and culture to continue.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four characteristics of West African Traditional Religion. [8 marks]
(b) State three reasons why it is important to study W.A.T.R. [6 marks]
(c) Mention one source from which knowledge of W.A.T.R. can be obtained. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) It has no known founder; it grew out of the people's experience over generations
2 marks: (a) It has no written scripture; beliefs are handed down orally and in arts
2 marks: (a) It is not a missionary religion; it is tied to a particular people and locality
2 marks: (a) It has a structure: belief in the Supreme Being, divinities, ancestors, spirits and mystical powers, and it pervades all of life
2 marks: (b) To understand and appreciate the cultural heritage of West Africans
2 marks: (b) To correct the wrong impressions created by early foreign writers
2 marks: (b) To promote tolerance and understanding between adherents of different religions
1 mark: (c) Any one: proverbs, myths, songs, names, drum language, carvings, shrines
questions.explanation: W.A.T.R. has no founder or written scripture, is not missionary and permeates all life; its structure has God at the top, then divinities, ancestors and spirits. Studying it helps learners appreciate their heritage, correct misconceptions and promote tolerance. Sources include proverbs, myths and carvings.

questions.topic: Terms Used to Describe West African Traditional Religion
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the terms (i) fetishism, (ii) animism and (iii) polytheism as used by early writers to describe W.A.T.R. [9 marks]
(b) Give two reasons why each of these terms is regarded as inappropriate. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Fetishism: worship of objects (fetishes) believed to possess magical power
3 marks: (a)(ii) Animism: belief that natural objects such as trees, rivers and rocks have souls or spirits
3 marks: (a)(iii) Polytheism: worship of many gods of more or less equal rank
2 marks: (b) Objects are symbols; worship is directed to spiritual beings, not to the objects themselves
2 marks: (b) Belief in spirits is only part of W.A.T.R.; the religion centres on a Supreme Being
2 marks: (b) The divinities are not equal to God but derive their power from him, so the religion is better seen as diffused monotheism
questions.explanation: Fetishism, animism and polytheism were coined by outsiders who misunderstood the religion. The objects are symbols, spirits are only part of the belief system, and the divinities are subordinate to one Supreme God.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe four qualifications a person must possess to become an ancestor. [8 marks]
(b) Explain four roles of the ancestors in the life of the family. [4 marks]
(c) Describe one way in which the living honour the ancestors. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) He must have lived to old age
2 marks: (a) He must have lived a morally upright life
2 marks: (a) He must have died a good (natural) death and been given proper burial rites
2 marks: (a) He must have had children
1 mark: (b) They protect the family from harm
1 mark: (b) They act as intermediaries between the living and God
1 mark: (b) They are custodians of family morals and punish wrongdoers
1 mark: (b) They bless the family with children, health and good harvest
3 marks: (c) Through libation and offerings at family shrines or at festivals, calling their names and asking for their blessing
questions.explanation: Ancestors are elders who lived long, morally upright lives, had children and died good deaths with full burial. They guard the family, uphold morality, intercede with God and bless their descendants; the living honour them with libation, offerings and remembrance.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three main features of worship in W.A.T.R. [9 marks]
(b) State three types of sacrifice and the purpose of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Prayer and libation: words of praise and requests, often while pouring water or drink
3 marks: (a) Sacrifice: offering of animals, food or drink to God, divinities or ancestors
3 marks: (a) Spirit possession/music and dance: the divinity takes over a medium to give messages; songs and drumming accompany worship
2 marks: (b) Thanksgiving sacrifice: to show gratitude for favours received
2 marks: (b) Propitiatory sacrifice: to appease an offended spiritual being
2 marks: (b) Votive sacrifice: to fulfil a vow, or preventive/foundation sacrifice to ward off evil
questions.explanation: Worship includes prayer with libation, sacrifice and spirit possession with music and dance. Sacrifices may be thanksgiving, propitiatory, votive, substitutionary or preventive, each serving to restore or maintain relationship with the spiritual world.

questions.stem:
(a) What is the attitude of W.A.T.R. to wealth? [5 marks]
(b) State four approved ways of acquiring wealth in traditional society. [4 marks]
(c) Explain three consequences of acquiring wealth through evil means. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Wealth is seen as a blessing from God and the ancestors when honestly acquired
2 marks: (a) The wealthy are expected to share with relatives and support the community
1 mark: (b) Hard work in farming
1 mark: (b) Trading
1 mark: (b) Craftwork such as weaving, carving or smithing
1 mark: (b) Inheritance or hunting/fishing
2 marks: (c) Punishment from the divinities and ancestors, such as illness or sudden death
2 marks: (c) Loss of respect and possible banishment from the community
2 marks: (c) The wealth does not last and may bring misfortune on the family
questions.explanation: Honest wealth is a blessing to be shared; it is gained by farming, trade, crafts and inheritance. Ill-gotten wealth brings divine punishment, disgrace and short-lived prosperity.

questions.topic: The Role of W.A.T.R. in Conflict Resolution and Management
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of conflict in West African traditional society. [3 marks]
(b) State three causes of conflict in traditional society. [6 marks]
(c) Describe three ways in which W.A.T.R. helps to resolve conflicts. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) A disagreement or struggle between individuals or groups over interests, rights or values which threatens communal peace
2 marks: (b) Disputes over land and boundaries
2 marks: (b) Chieftaincy and succession disputes
2 marks: (b) Marital/family quarrels or inheritance disputes
2 marks: (c) Mediation and arbitration by elders and chiefs
2 marks: (c) Oath-taking before divinities to establish the truth
2 marks: (c) Covenants and reconciliation rites such as sharing kola nut and sacrifices to restore peace
questions.explanation: Conflict is a clash of interests that disturbs communal harmony, often over land, chieftaincy or family matters. Traditional religion resolves it through elders' arbitration, oaths before divinities, covenants and reconciliation rituals.
